questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements regarding energy consideration in reference to Bernoulli's principle:
1. Pitot tube indicates the position of total energy line above any arbitrary datum.
2. In rotational flow, velocity varies normal to the flow.
3. The piezometric head in a uniform pipe does not remain constant in the direction normal to the flow for rotational flow.
4. In a real fluid, the total head varies throughout the normal section in a uniform pipe.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
(b)
Statement 3 is incorrect. Piezometric head in a uniform pipe remain constant in a direction normal to flow for rotational flow.

questions.qtext: As compared to a streamlined body, a bluff body will have

options.text: more pressure drag and more friction drag
less pressure drag and less friction drag
more pressure drag and less friction drag
more friction drag and less pressure drag

questions.solution:
(c)
Bluff body is the one which gives rise to large wakes at the rear end that pressure drag in much higher than the friction drag.

questions.qtext:
While analyzing a general qualitative analogy between the gas dynamics and the open channel flow, which of the following results are correct?
1. Froude's number is analogous to Mach number.
2. Water depth is analogous to gas density.
3. Water depth is analogous to gas pressure.
4. Hydraulic jumps are analogous to gas shock waves.
questions.solution:
(d)
Statement 3 is false. Square of water depth is analogous to gas pressure.

Consider the following statements:
1. Dilatant fluid is shear thickening fluid increasing its resistance with increasing strain rate.
2. Pseudoplastic fluid is shear thickening fluid and is less resistant to high strain rates.
3. Rheopectic fluids require a gradually increasing shear stress to maintain a constant strain rate.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
Statement 2 is false. Pseudoplastic fluid is a shear thinning fluid.

questions.qtext:
Nikuradse's test results are plotted on a logarithmic scale with friction factor f as ordinate and
Reynold's number Re as abscissa. Choose the correct statements:
1. For Re < 2000, friction factor follows a linear relationship with Re.
2. For high values of Re and pipes with very small relative roughness, friction factor is governed by Re and thickness of laminar sub-layer.
3. In rough turbulent flow, f versus Re relationship becomes parallel to Re axis.
questions.solution:
(a)
Statement 2 is false. For high values of Re and pipes with very small relative roughness, friction factor is governed by Re only.

questions.qtext:
Choose the correct statements for flow occurring from left to right:
1. If streamlines are straight and diverging then only convective tangential positive acceleration exists.
2. If streamlines are curved and equidistant then there will be only normal convective acceleration.
3. If streamlines are curved and converging then both normal and tangential acceleration exist.
4. If streamlines are straight and parallel to each other then there is no acceleration.
questions.solution:
(b)
Statement 1 is false. If streamlines are straight and diverging then only convective tangential
retardation i.e. negative acceleration exists.

Statement (I): Provision of air vessels on the suction and delivery side of the reciprocating pump increases the delivery head of the pump.
Statement (II): Air vessels reduce the acceleration head and makes the discharge uniform.
questions.solution:
(b)
Air vessels save lot of work required to be done against the frictional resistance in suction and
delivery pipes and thus, delivery head increases.

Statement (I): Kaplan turbine maintains high efficiency over a wide range of turbine output.
Statement (II): Vanes on the hub of Kaplan turbine are adjustable.
questions.solution:
(a)
In Kaplan turbine, vanes are adjustable whose position can be varied with load on the turbine and thus discharge. As the blades are adjusted for the shock entry of flow, high efficiency is maintained over a wide range of turbine output.
